recipes.name: Classic Dinner Rolls
ingredients_raw: 2 cups all-purpose flour, divided, or as needed

steps.text: Combine ¾ cup flour, sugar, undissolved yeast, and salt in a large bowl.
Heat milk, water, and 2 tablespoons butter in a saucepan until very warm (120 degrees to 130 degrees F).

Add warm milk mixture to the flour mixture. Beat for 2 minutes on medium speed of an electric mixer, scraping the bowl occasionally. Add ¼ cup flour; beat for 2 minutes at high speed. Stir in enough remaining flour to make soft dough.
Knead dough on a lightly floured surface until smooth and elastic, about 8 to 10 minutes. Cover; let rest for 10 minutes.

Shape pieces into balls and place in a greased 8-inch round pan. Cover and let rise in warm, draft-free place until doubled in size, about 30 minutes. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Bake rolls in the preheated oven until golden brown on top, about 20 minutes.
Brush with melted butter if you like.

raw_recipe.headline: Classic Dinner Rolls
raw_recipe.description: These soft, fluffy dinner rolls are simple to make from scratch and irresistible served warm from the oven for the perfect addition to any meal.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make soft and fluffy dinner rolls from scratch. These dinner rolls are fluffy, buttery, and a bit sweet for a perfect flavor combination, and the recipe uses pantry staple ingredients including flour, yeast, sugar, salt, warm milk, and butter. The rolls are best served warm with melted butter brushed on top and are the perfect companion for any meal. Trust us — no one will be able to say no to these rolls when they're warm right out of the oven.

review.reviewBody: The rolls turned out beautifully, light tender crumb. I proofed my yeast with the water and sugar before adding the other ingredients, mixing it by hand and not with a mixer, I also used half all-purpose flour and half bread flour. I only had active yeast, not the rapid rise, so I allowed an hour or so for the first rise, then gently formed a log and cut 12 pieces with my bench scraper and loosely placed them in the cake pan then let them rise another hour. Love the way they turned out, next time I will add a bit more salt, but other then that wonderful!

I didn't exactly make changes to the recipe but added something that was my favorite. This recipe like it is ......let's just say couldn't be better. Loved it but made a few additions because of the Holidays. I always brush my hot rolls with butter which this recipe called for too; then sprinkled them with oregano and then drizzled butter again and then sprinkled with freshly grated Parmesan Cheese. They are perfect either way. It's a keeper for sure. I let them rise twice. They were delicious.

I did a test on Monday. Wow. Thanksgiving morning I made 8 dozen. One for my family and 7 for the community free Thanksgiving dinner put on my a local church. Delicious. I didn't work that hard though. I cut up the butter into small pieces, adding to it the milk and the water. Microwaved on high for one minute. Put it in my bread machine with the dry ingredients. Set it to dough. Took it out after the first rise. Put my oven on warm for a few minutes then shut it off. Formed the rolls then put in the oven to rise. After rising I turned the oven on 375 and set the timer to 20 minutes. Turned out perfect. Thanks!!!

Absolute perfection. During the kneeding process I added cheddar cheese. I preheated my oven to 200 then turned it off and cracked the door, allowed rolls to rest for 10 min. Then separated into balls and allowed them to rise in warm oven for 30 min. Baked for 18 minutes and topped with herbs and butter. Perfection!

I used 3 tablespoons of butter and added my rapid rise yeast to the milk/water/butter mixture. After about 10mins I added the rest of the ingredients. I let it rise for about 20-30mins and then ripped it into 12 pieces and let it rise in the baking pan for another 20-30mins till almost doubled in size. Then I gave it an egg yolk and milk wash before baking for about 17mins.

Amazing!! I used heavy cream and almond milk combined in place of the milk. Used a full stick of butter with the end like a paintbrush to slather on butter straight out of the oven. This softened the brown tops and made them SO GOOD. I also doubled the recipe and weight out 3.2 ounce balls of dough that I formed by gathering the edges into a pinched fold underneath, for a smooth round top. They were big! I used bread flour instead of AP. Mixed it up in my kitchenaid but kneaded by hand also until I was satisfied... I also accidently overproofed them for the last rise but they are very forgiving and turned out so well. It's a staple recipe now!

I have made these a few times now and they are always perfect. I do use the traditional yeast though (2 1/4 tsp). I warm the milk, butter, sugar and salt until the butter melts and then proof the yeast in 1/4 cup of warm water with about 1/2 tsp. of sugar and then add to the warm milk mixture and then add flour as needed and knead by hand. I let it rise for one hour, form into balls (after weighing them) and let them rise for one more hour. For those that are saying they are getting biscuits or hockey pucks, maybe check that your yeast is not too old?

My family absolutely fell in love with these rolls. My babies(grandbabies) beg to make these every time they come. These are the best and easiest to make. Definitely a keeper and crowd pleaser. We've also incorporated a little to ours we've added melted butter and a cinnamon sugar mixture to them making Cinnamon drops. Just roll them in the butter place cinnamon sugar mixture in ziplock bag and drop rolls into bag and shake gently. Remove and serve with homemade glaze

I made a double batch, and they were excellent! On the second batch, I warmed the wet ingredients to 'hottish warm' to the touch and added the yeast. Let it sit for 5 mins, then add to dry ingredients. The second batch did get a better rise—fantastic, classic flavour, pulling apart and watching the steam come out mmmm!! Just for fun, I sprinkled Garlic Plus on the tops before baking. Excellent pair with beef and barley soup!

It was good with a couple of minor changes I cut the sugar in half, I only let the temp of the liquids get to 110 F so it doesn't kill the yeast, and in step 4 I placed the dough back in the bowl and sprayed canola oil lightly on it and covered it and let it double in size which took about 30 minutes. I also cooked them in a rectangle pan instead of a round pan. Came out great!

I just made this recipe using regular yeast letting it rise for one hour first, then rounding out approx 9 balls and let them rise for one more hour. They came out great! Will definitely be making again.
What did i like? Everything. Easy to follow & execute and they turned out great! Golden brown, fluffy, delicious!

Oh. My. Goodness. 5/5 for me! The recipe is totally fool-proof and incredibly delicious! I used pizza yeast instead of rapid rise and the results were amazing. So glad to have found an easy recipe for dinners! :)
I used my bread maker to make the dough. This is so easy and uses simple ingredients. So fluffy and addictive. My family ate them all in one night. Made 12 good size rolls.
Very easy to make. Family enjoyed them.
Turned out excellent. Made them straight from the recipe.

Not surprising, this is the recipe from Fleischmann's website (given they are credited as a co-author). I used active yeast. I made these plant based (Almond milk and plant based butter). Very nice fluffy bun. Will make again. Excellent for sopping up gravy!!!
Worked wonderfully and how a household staple. I add dried rosemary for a bit extra flavor but plain is also amazing.

The Recipe is very easy to follow; I. did not make any changes to recipe。 The ingredient is very simple and easy to follow。 I enjoy eating dinner rolls specially during the Holiday Season。 The time frame was the same for preparing and baking 1 hour and 35 minutes。 These Dinner Rolls are Absolutely Delicious with melted butter

I think a touch more sugar would be good. But they rose perfect. I mixed all the dry into my bread maker then added the butter, milk, and water while it turning to mix . Let it mix for 12 mins then divided it up and let it rise for 30 mins.
